skill.name: tanstack-query
skill.description: Guides React teams through TanStack Query v5 setup, migration, data fetching, mutations, caching, SSR hydration, DevTools, and testing patterns.
skill.summary: Build and debug TanStack Query v5 workflows for React applications.
skill.author: jezweb

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, TypeScript template literals, local API examples, and React identifiers. Confirmed issues are low-risk external demo API calls in copy-ready templates, plus medium-risk semantic concerns around production DevTools exposure and visible stack traces.

remediation.issue: Production DevTools example lacks an enforced auth gate.
remediation.suggestion: Wrap production DevTools behind role-based authentication and a server-controlled feature flag, or remove the production example from copy-ready templates.

remediation.issue: Default error boundary can expose stack traces to users.
remediation.suggestion: Show generic production errors in the UI and send stack traces only to a trusted error reporting service.

remediation.issue: Copy-ready templates use public demo API endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Use placeholder base URLs or local mock handlers, and clearly require endpoint replacement before using real data.

remediation.issue: Placeholder shell script ships with the skill.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the unused script or document that it is nonfunctional, so installers do not see an unnecessary executable artifact.

semantic_findings.title: Production DevTools Can Expose Cache Data
semantic_findings.description: The production DevTools example loads and renders React Query DevTools when a local showDevTools flag is true, but the sample does not enforce authentication. Query cache data can include user records, tokens, or API responses if copied into production.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly labels the section as production DevTools and renders the component from a local toggle only. The same file later warns not to ship production DevTools without authentication.

semantic_findings.title: Error Boundary Displays Stack Traces
semantic_findings.description: The default fallback renders error.message and error.stack in the page. Production users could see implementation details if this template is copied without an environment guard.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly renders error details and the stack trace inside the visible fallback UI. This is useful during development but can leak internal details in production.

content.user_title: Build TanStack Query v5 React Workflows
content.value_statement: TanStack Query v5 changes can break data fetching, mutations, and SSR behavior. This skill provides focused setup, migration, debugging, and template guidance for React teams.
actual_capabilities: Explains QueryClient setup, provider wiring, cache timing, and DevTools configuration.
Provides useQuery, useMutation, useInfiniteQuery, and custom hook patterns for React.
Helps migrate v4 code to v5 object syntax, gcTime, isPending, and placeholderData.
Documents optimistic updates, invalidation, retry behavior, and network mode choices.
Covers SSR hydration issues, suspense queries, and streaming server component caveats.
Includes testing guidance with MSW handlers and isolated QueryClient instances.
limitations: It does not install packages or modify projects automatically.
Examples use demo endpoints and must be adapted before production use.
It focuses on React usage, not every TanStack Query framework adapter.
Version notes may need review when TanStack Query releases new breaking changes.

use_cases.title: Set up a React app
use_cases.description: Create a QueryClient, wrap the app provider, configure cache defaults, and add DevTools safely.

use_cases.title: Migrate from v4 to v5
use_cases.description: Replace removed callbacks, update option names, fix status flags, and resolve TypeScript migration errors.

use_cases.title: Debug server state behavior
use_cases.description: Investigate refetching, invalidation, optimistic updates, pagination, suspense, and hydration problems.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add TanStack Query v5 to a React TypeScript app. Include provider setup, sensible defaults, and DevTools guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Create query hooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Design TanStack Query v5 hooks for this resource. Include query keys, queryOptions, staleTime, error handling, and loading states.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate v4 code
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React Query v4 usage and convert it to TanStack Query v5. Explain each breaking change and safer replacement.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose advanced behavior

output_examples.input: A team reports stale data after a mutation.

best_practices: Use stable query keys and central query option factories for repeated resources.
Prefer explicit invalidation and optimistic rollback paths for mutations.
Review DevTools, stack traces, and demo endpoints before shipping production code.
anti_patterns: Do not use removed v4 callbacks on useQuery in new v5 code.
Do not expose production DevTools or cache contents without authentication.
Do not copy demo API endpoints into applications that handle real user data.

faq.question: Does this skill run TanStack Query code for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and templates that you adapt inside your own React project.

faq.question: Which TanStack Query version does it target?
faq.answer: It targets TanStack Query v5 and includes notes for common v4 to v5 migration issues.

faq.question: Can it help with TypeScript errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers queryOptions, typed query keys, mutation state, error types, and common v5 type changes.

faq.question: Does it cover SSR and hydration?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for suspense, streaming server components, hydration timing, and related known issues.

faq.question: Are the templates production ready?
faq.answer: They are starting points. Replace demo endpoints, remove unsafe debugging output, and review authentication needs.

faq.question: Can it help write tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes MSW handlers, per-test QueryClient setup, retries, and cache isolation patterns.
